items.requirement: Define the exact production responsibility of Elastic virtualization.
Document what Elastic virtualization owns and explicitly does not own.
Identify upstream, downstream, and peer dependencies of Elastic virtualization.
Define the authoritative source of truth used by Elastic virtualization.
Document assumptions Elastic virtualization makes about nodes, runtimes, networks, storage, and control planes.
Define tenant, environment, site, and workload boundaries relevant to Elastic virtualization.
Separate mandatory Elastic virtualization capabilities from optional optimizations.
Document unsupported deployment patterns and non-goals for Elastic virtualization.
Assign an accountable owner and escalation path for Elastic virtualization.
Approve an architecture decision record for Elastic virtualization, its technologies (HyperFlux), and its function (Microsecond-scale vCPU/core reassignment).
Translate the source function of Elastic virtualization — Microsecond-scale vCPU/core reassignment — into testable SHALL-level requirements.
Define functional requirements for Elastic virtualization across cloud, datacenter, near-edge, and far-edge contexts where applicable.
Define non-functional requirements for latency, availability, durability, consistency, isolation, or determinism as applicable.
Define success, partial success, degraded operation, retryable failure, and terminal failure semantics for Elastic virtualization.
Define lifecycle states and legal state transitions managed or exposed by Elastic virtualization.
Define versioning and backward-compatibility requirements for Elastic virtualization.
Define capacity ceilings, quotas, and fairness semantics relevant to Elastic virtualization.
Define behavior when network connectivity is intermittent or absent.
Define precedence rules when Elastic virtualization requirements conflict with security, residency, SLO, or cost constraints.
Maintain a requirements traceability matrix from each Elastic virtualization requirement to implementation and verification evidence.
Enumerate every API, WIT contract, RPC, event, file, device, hypervisor, or control-plane boundary exposed by Elastic virtualization.
Use versioned typed schemas for all externally visible Elastic virtualization contracts.
Define authentication requirements at each Elastic virtualization boundary.
Define authorization and explicit capability requirements at each Elastic virtualization boundary.
Define timeout, cancellation, retry, idempotency, and backpressure semantics for Elastic virtualization.
Define structured failure codes and machine-readable error details for Elastic virtualization.
Define compatibility behavior when peers use different supported versions.
Document payload, concurrency, queue, connection, or resource limits at Elastic virtualization interfaces.
Provide reference examples and conformance fixtures for Elastic virtualization.
Create automated integration tests proving Elastic virtualization interoperates with adjacent architectural layers.
Select and pin approved implementations, versions, or specifications for Elastic virtualization: HyperFlux.
Separate immutable artifacts from mutable configuration and state for Elastic virtualization.
Define declarative configuration and secure defaults for Elastic virtualization.
Validate configuration before activation and fail closed on security-critical errors.
Support site- and environment-specific configuration without rebuilding immutable artifacts.
Record configuration provenance, version, author, and activation time.
Apply atomic or transactional configuration updates where partial application is unsafe.
Define automatic and operator-driven rollback for failed Elastic virtualization changes.
Keep credentials and secret material out of ordinary Elastic virtualization configuration and diagnostics.
Provide a deterministic bootstrap path from an empty node/environment to healthy Elastic virtualization operation.
Threat-model Elastic virtualization against malicious tenants, compromised workloads, hostile inputs, supply-chain compromise, and control-plane abuse.
Apply least privilege to every identity and capability used by Elastic virtualization.
Eliminate ambient filesystem, network, device, kernel, and secret authority wherever Elastic virtualization permits.
Authenticate nodes, peers, artifacts, providers, and control-plane actors before trust is granted.
Verify signatures, digests, provenance, and approved versions for executable or policy artifacts consumed by Elastic virtualization.
Enforce tenant/workload isolation across Elastic virtualization execution, memory, state, network, and device boundaries as applicable.
Encrypt sensitive Elastic virtualization data in transit and at rest with managed key rotation.
Define safe behavior when identity, attestation, policy, key, or time services are unavailable.
Emit tamper-evident audit events for security-sensitive Elastic virtualization operations.
Run adversarial tests for privilege escalation, injection, replay, spoofing, escape, side channels, and resource exhaustion.
Enumerate component, process, VM, node, site, network, provider, dependency, and control-plane failures affecting Elastic virtualization.
Define automated health and stall detection thresholds for Elastic virtualization.
Implement bounded retry with backoff and jitter only where operations are safe to retry.
Implement admission control, load shedding, or circuit breaking to prevent Elastic virtualization failure cascades.
Define failover behavior without violating isolation, residency, or consistency requirements.
Provide degraded operation when noncritical dependencies are unavailable.
Define crash-consistency, restart, resume, or replay semantics for mutable Elastic virtualization state.
Protect against split-brain, duplicate ownership, stale controllers, or duplicate execution where relevant.
Provide quarantine, freeze, disable, or isolation controls for unsafe Elastic virtualization behavior.
Run fault-injection tests proving Elastic virtualization recovery against documented objectives.
Establish reproducible baselines for Elastic virtualization latency, throughput, startup, CPU, memory, storage, network, and power overhead.
Define p50, p95, p99, and worst-case performance thresholds for Elastic virtualization.
Measure Elastic virtualization under steady load, burst load, overload, scale-out, scale-in, and recovery.
Measure per-workload and per-tenant overhead introduced by Elastic virtualization.
Identify avoidable serialization, copies, context switches, network hops, duplicated images, or duplicated state in Elastic virtualization.
Apply locality, caching, direct composition, batching, zero-copy, or kernel-bypass optimizations where semantics permit.
Bound memory growth, queue depth, buffer size, concurrency, and resource fan-out.
Measure power and thermal impact on constrained edge nodes where relevant.
Define capacity models and saturation signals that predict when Elastic virtualization needs more resources.
Block releases that regress approved Elastic virtualization startup, density, throughput, or tail-latency thresholds.
Expose Elastic virtualization health, readiness, version, configuration, dependency status, and active capability set.
Emit structured metrics for rate, errors, latency, saturation, backlog, and resource use.
Emit structured logs with stable node, tenant, workload, component, and operation identifiers.
Propagate trace context across all relevant Elastic virtualization boundaries.
Expose high-cardinality diagnostic detail safely without leaking tenant or secret data.
Record the reason for every automated decision made by Elastic virtualization.
Provide an operator-readable explain view linking decisions to input state, policies, topology, and constraints.
Correlate Elastic virtualization events with application release lineage and the live infrastructure graph.
Define telemetry retention, sampling, privacy, and export policy.
Create dashboards and alerts distinguishing ordinary load, degradation, policy rejection, dependency failure, attack, and software defect.
Create unit tests for deterministic Elastic virtualization logic and state transitions.
Create contract tests for every public Elastic virtualization interface.
Create integration tests with every supported adjacent layer and execution tier.
Create compatibility tests across supported CPU architectures, runtimes, hypervisors, providers, and protocol versions relevant to Elastic virtualization.
Fuzz parsers, schemas, protocol handlers, WIT/RPC boundaries, or untrusted inputs handled by Elastic virtualization.
Create concurrency and race-condition tests for shared/distributed Elastic virtualization state.
Create security tests derived directly from the Elastic virtualization threat model.
Create benchmark, soak, burst, and fleet-scale tests appropriate to Elastic virtualization.
Create disaster, partition, reconnect, and degraded-control-plane tests.
Require machine-readable acceptance evidence before certifying a Elastic virtualization release for production.
Define production SLOs, error budgets, and support commitments for Elastic virtualization.
Define canary, staged rollout, rollback, and emergency-disable procedures for Elastic virtualization.
Maintain a supported-version compatibility matrix for Elastic virtualization and adjacent dependencies.
Define patching, vulnerability response, and end-of-life SLAs for Elastic virtualization.
Provide backup, restore, migration, or reconstruction procedures for Elastic virtualization state where applicable.
Create day-0 bootstrap, day-1 deployment, and day-2 operation runbooks.
Define incident severity, paging, escalation, containment, and recovery procedures.
Perform recurring access, policy, dependency, configuration, and architecture reviews.
Track exceptions, waivers, technical debt, and deprecated behaviors with owners and expiry dates.
Require a formal production exit gate confirming architecture, requirements, interfaces, implementation, security, resilience, performance, observability, testing, rollback, and ownership readiness.
